events.title: Understanding Latin America’s Economy in the Twenty-first Century
events.description:
Latin America’s economic performance is often depicted as a long sequence of repeated failures, including its contribution to global financial crises as well as its slow growth and intractable inequalities. Its experience in the twenty-first century, however, reveals considerable and underappreciated successes (as well as setbacks). This talk will review the region's growth and development in the last quarter century, including the commodity boom, a surprising decline in economic inequality, responses to the financial and Covid-19 crises, and the emergence of left-leaning governments that opted for pragmatic and orthodox macro policies mixed with innovative antipoverty programs.

Livestream Link

Jeff Dayton-Johnson has served as vice president of academic affairs and dean at the Middlebury Institute of International Studies at Monterey since 2014. He is also a professor of international policy & development there. Prior to joining MIIS, he was senior economist for Latin America & the Caribbean at the OECD Development Centre in Paris, and assistant and associate professor of economics and international development studies at Dalhousie University in Canada. Dayton-Johnson's research and teaching interests include economic development, inequality, Latin America & the Caribbean, public policy, migration, social cohesion. He earned a PhD in economics and an AB hons in Latin American Studies at UC Berkeley.

events.title: PhD Dissertation Defense: Santiago Mille Fragoso
events.description:
Title: Computational and Synthetic Design of Modular Molecular Devices

Abstract: Cells use molecular mechanisms to detect environmental signals and convert them into functional responses. Engineering this capability could enable programmable cell behaviors, diagnostics, and therapies, yet these sensors remain difficult to adapt to new inputs and outputs. I propose new strategies for designing molecular devices, introducing methods to design binders to proteins of interest (POIs) and a post-transcriptional mechanism that converts the binding of a molecule into an output, thereby contributing complementary approaches to program the sensing, processing, and actuation layers of synthetic molecular sensors. First, I present LIDAR (Ligand-Induced Dimerization Activating RNA editing), a post-transcriptional receptor platform that couples ligand-dependent protein proximity to ADAR-mediated RNA editing. LIDAR functions across architectures and ligand classes to produce functional outputs. Second, I present Germinal, a computational pipeline for designing antibodies for therapeutic and synthetic biology applications. By jointly optimizing antibody structure and sequence with AlphaFold-Multimer and an antibody language model, I generated VHH and scFv binders against four proteins using tens of tested designs per target, with structural and mutational analyses confirming their binding modes. Finally, I outline how these advances could converge in LIDAR-inspired synthetic receptors that couple antibody-based recognition of intracellular proteins to RNA editing. Together, these two projects establish a path toward modular molecular devices whose inputs and outputs can be selected by design.

Please contact Sofia Rakicevic-More for the Zoom link.

events.title: Zeming Lin and Roshan Rao from Biohub - Day 1
events.description:
More info for both days and livestream links at broad.io/biohub-broad-2026. 

 

Thursday, October 29

Title: World models of protein biology
Location: Broad Auditorium (415M-1-Auditorium)
Time: 11:00 am - 12:00 pm
Speaker: Zeming Lin, Biohub


Abstract: Protein language models learn representations of sequence and structure that support the prediction of biomolecular complexes and the design of proteins with experimentally measured binding activity. Biohub's open release of the ESM family of world models – ESMC, ESMFold2, and ESM Atlas – makes these capabilities available to the broader research community. Using ESMC and ESMFold2 to search candidate sequences, the team designed minibinders and single-chain antibodies against five targets. Additional inference-time search improved experimental hit rates in nine of ten target-modality comparisons. The ESMAtlas gives a perspective on scientific discovery with interpretable ESM features.

These advances make structure prediction and large-scale computational search increasingly accessible, while experimental validation remains a central constraint on biological discovery. Model confidence can help prioritize candidates, but establishing binding, specificity, and function requires experimental evidence. The cost and timescale of obtaining that evidence limit how rapidly computational hypotheses can be evaluated and refined. In this talk, Zeming Lin will examine how researchers can use these models for prediction and design, and how virtual biology might accelerate experimental throughput.

Biography: Zeming Lin is a Principal Research Scientist in AI Research at Biohub and a co-founder of EvolutionaryScale. His research focuses on large-scale protein models for structure prediction and protein design. He was the main modeling contributor to ESMFold, which predicts atomic-level protein structures directly from sequence, and helped develop ESM3 and Biohub's recent ESMFold2. Bio: Carlos Gabriel Corpuz, MD, MBA, is an Infectious Diseases fellow at the University of Washington and an MPH student in Epidemiology. His research examines the implementation of long-acting injectable antiretroviral therapy across HIV care settings, with a focus on reaching patients with viremia, equitable access, and treatment outcomes. events.title: Children and Childhood in Colonial Senegal - Kelly Duke Bryant
events.description:
How did French colonial institutions seek to define, regulate, and ‘‘protect’’ childhood in Senegal, and how did children respond? 

In this talk based on her recent book, Negotiating Childhood: French Colonialism and African Children in Senegal, 1848–1940, Kelly Duke Bryant explores the lived realities of African children across courts, schools, streets, reformatories, vaccine clinics, and other sites of colonial intervention. Rather than treating children as passive subjects, Bryant illuminates the ways children limited or negotiated colonial reforms and how the colonial state’s reliance on cooperation produced unexpected forms of resistance and accommodation. The talk highlights long-term consequences of colonial governance, such as the privileging of chronological age and the centrality of official documentation, that continue to shape Senegalese childhoods.

Speaker Details

Kelly Duke Bryant is chair of the History Department at Rowan University, where she has taught since 2009. She earned her MA in history from the University of Wisconsin and her Ph.D., also in history, from Johns Hopkins University. A specialist in the history of West Africa, she has published scholarly articles and book chapters on the history of education, childhood, and youth in colonial Senegal. She is the author of two books, Education as Politics: Colonial Schooling and Political Debate in Senegal, 1850s-1914 (University of Wisconsin Press, 2015) and Negotiating Childhood: French Colonialism and African Children in Senegal, 1848-1940 (University of Massachusetts Press, 2026). She recently began a term as president of the French Colonial Historical Society.

events.title: Alcohol-Associated Hepatitis and Early Liver Transplantation
events.description:
OverviewThis activity reviews the diagnosis and management of alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) and alcohol-associated hepatitis (AAH), including alcohol cessation strategies, treatment of alcohol use disorder, appropriate use of corticosteroids, and the evolving role of early liver transplantation. Learners will gain practical guidance on risk stratification, treatment thresholds, and timely referral of patients with severe alcohol-associated liver disease.

RegistrationRegistration for all practitioners - free.

To register for this activity, please click HERE

CreditsAMA PRA Category 1 Credits™ (1.00 hours), AAPA Category 1 CME credits (1.00 hours), ANCC Contact Hours (1.00 hours), Non-Physician Participation Credit (1.00 hours)

Target AudienceSpecialties - Family Medicine & Community Health, Gastroenterology, Gastroenterology & Hepatology, Hematology, Internal MedicineProfessions - Advance Practice Nurse (APN), Non-Physician, Nurse, Physician, Physician Associate, Registered Nurse (RN) ObjectivesAt the conclusion of this activity, learners should be able to:
1. Apply NIAAA clinical criteria and phosphatidylethanol testing to accurately diagnose alcohol-associated hepatitis and distinguish alcohol-associated liver disease from MASLD.
2. Use MELD rather than the Maddrey discriminant function to risk-stratify patients with alcohol-associated hepatitis and identify candidates for corticosteroid therapy.
3. Manage corticosteroid therapy appropriately, including assessment of contraindications and calculation of the Lille score at day 4 or 7 to discontinue treatment in non-responders.
4. Initiate concurrent treatment of alcohol use disorder using behavioral support and evidence-based pharmacotherapy, avoiding agents contraindicated in liver disease.
5. Identify patients appropriate for early liver transplant referral without applying a fixed 6-month sobriety interval, and document eligibility using specific, non-stigmatizing language.

World AMR Awareness Week 2026: One Health, One Action: Prevent AMR Now
Make a Gutsy Move for Better Health
events.description:
The gut microbiome is a diverse colony of bacteria that resides in each of us. Emerging research shows these bacteria play a key role in a healthy immune system. They are also associated with conditions such as obesity, diabetes, irritable bowel syndrome, depression, and a variety of cancers. Yet most of us don’t know much about gut health or what to do to improve it.

In this noontime webinar, you will be introduced to this secret world inside each of us through evidence-based research related to gut health. You will learn how the microbiota within the gut function, including their role in health promotion and disease. We will discuss the difference between prebiotics and probiotics and identify sources in food and supplements. We will also address the role of nutrition in supporting the microbiome and the practical steps you can take now to support your gut health and improve your well-being.

This class will be recorded and a one-week link to the recording will be shared with all registered participants. 

To receive incentive points, attend at least 80% of the live session or listen to the entire recording within one week.

Request disability accommodations and access info.

Class details are subject to change.

events.title: Stanford Emergency Medicine Innovation Symposium - StEMI X
events.description:
AI is reshaping diagnosis. Digital health is redefining access. Acute care is evolving fast.

The Stanford Emergency Medicine Innovation Symposium - StEMI X - brings together the clinicians, technologists, operators, investors, and policymakers who are building what comes next. StEMI X is the first and largest virtual global conference on innovation in acute care.CME will be offered for attendance. Shiv Rao, MD, founder and CEO of Abridge will offer the keynote, joined by 30+ expert speakers from around the country.

Sessions include:

The Augmented ED: Leveling Up Your Clinical Practice with Next-Gen AI

The AI Minefield: Navigating Ethics, Bias, and Safety in Clinical Care

See One, Do One, Teach One, Prompt One: Medical Education in the AI Era

Co-Pilot or Replacement? Reclaiming the Physician’s Role in the Age of AI

Year in Review: Top 10 acute care technology research papers of 2026

Signal vs. Noise: What's Real and What's Not in the Next Generation of Medical Hardware

Building Safer Waiting Rooms: Using Tech to Solve the "Right Patient, Right Time" Puzzle

Telemedicine in Acute Care: From the ED to the Home

Design Thinking in the ED: Turning frontline insight into better solutions

The Innovation Ecosystem: Bridging the Gap Between Industry and the Front Lines

Bedside to Boardroom: A Blueprint for Building a High-Impact Acute Care Startup

Winning the C-Suite: The Art of securing institutional buy-in for emerging technologies
